title: Claude Code helped me make my 1,000-wishlist video: a horde spells the number, then the game's own fire burns it
author: CrisosDev
selftext:
Just Dying (solo dev) just passed 1,000 wishlists, so I made a celebration clip with Claude Code working inside the game's repo. The terrain, the goblins and the fire effects are all the game's own. What Claude did: it scripted the formation (the goblins run in and spell "1,000 WISHLISTS"), a camera move that pulls back to reveal it, and it triggered the game's existing VFX that burn the environment. Then, because I didn't want to re-record, it rendered the game's own animations for 19 characters on transparent frames and composited them around the screen, copying the timing of my existing Gerier peek animation.



What I found interesting is where it struggled. It can't judge layout the way I do. It put characters on top of Gerier, and a blurred background that looked awful to me looked fine to it. Every fix was me looking at the frames and telling it what was off, which made the job feel more like art direction than prompting. It also can't hear, so the music is my call.



How do you handle visual feedback loops with agents? Do you screenshot and describe, or have you found a way to let it check the result itself?



Free demo and wishlist in the first comment.
